output.brief: The rejections came from a data error in the new documentation system. The mandarin product record was copied from the avocado record on 1 Aug, and the 7.0°C avocado carriage temperature was never changed. Our spec is 4.0°C. Every Meridane container booked through the new system (K3, K4, K6, K8, K9) was set to 7.0°C and ran at that temperature, and all five were rejected. The Meridane container booked by email at 4.0°C (K1) and all three Coastway containers (K2, K5, K7) ran at 4°C and passed. That includes containers packed with the new fungicide. The temperature logs match our own loggers, so Meridane did what we told it to. The new fungicide, Lower Serra fruit and the transshipment route do not explain the pattern. Lower Serra pallets were worse inside the rejected containers, but the fruit was only 28–40% of each container, and the survey never covered the accepted ones. Do not suspend Lower Serra growers, claim against Meridane, or switch fungicide. First, correct the temperature in the mandarin record today. Ask Meridane to reset the container at sea (sailed 3 Oct) and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a check of reefer settings against the product spec before each submission. Loggers are a reasonable extra. Any recovery from the contractor should wait for a proper review, because our own sign-off also missed the error. Confidence is high.
